title: Why Branches Are Essential in Git

scenes.say: Why does Git use branches? What’s the big deal?

scenes.label: Commit
scenes.sub: A commit is a snapshot of your code at a point in time.
scenes.say: A commit is a snapshot of your code at a point in time.
Branches are pointers to commits. They let you work in parallel, like with feature branches. HEAD marks where you are now.
To combine branches, use merge or rebase. Merge keeps history and creates a merge commit. Rebase rewrites history for a cleaner, linear sequence.

scenes.title: Resolving Conflicts
scenes.say: When changes overlap, Git marks conflicts. You must edit the files to resolve them before finishing a merge or rebase.

scenes.question: Can you rebase a shared branch?
scenes.right: No—rebasing shared branches rewrites history and risks lost commits.
scenes.say: Can you rebase a shared branch? No—rebasing shared branches rewrites history and risks lost commits.
